Rule: Total debit must equal total credit on every journal header before posting.
A journal header must have at least two lines and at least one debit and one credit line.
A single journal line may carry a debit or a credit, never both, and never zero.
Origin: File 2 integrity counter "Lines with both Dr & Cr"

Rule: Posting is permitted only to accounts flagged Posting AND Active. Non-posting parents (112100, 115030) and inactive accounts (112031, 112036) are rejected.
Project and cost centre are mandatory on every journal line.
Origin: File 1 ledger — 1,195 of 1,195 rows carry a project

Rule: A cash or bank account (111xxx) may only be used with a cash_account_id, and any line touching 111xxx must carry one.
A line touching an advance account (112010, 112020, 112021, 112030, 112032, 112035, 112037) must carry an advance holder or counterparty.
A counterparty is mandatory on payable, receivable, advance, shareholder and revenue lines.
Posting into a period whose status is Final Close or Locked is rejected.
The journal number is system-generated, unique per entity and fiscal year, and gapless within the sequence.
A direct-payment-by-shareholder entry (TT-02) may not touch any 111xxx cash account.
The transaction date may not be later than the posting date, and the posting date must fall inside the selected accounting period.
Document status is mandatory on every journal header and takes one of Complete, Partial or Missing. Partial and Missing raise an open exception that cannot be closed by deletion.
A document reference is mandatory when document status is Complete.
A historical entry with no date in the source carries date_status = NO DATE IN SOURCE and posts with a null transaction date. The system must never substitute a date.
A user may not approve an entry he created (maker–checker separation).
Only a user with the Post permission may post, and only an Approved entry may be posted.
A posted entry may not be edited or deleted under any circumstance.
Amounts are stored as integer IQD. Decimal input is rejected while the no-decimals policy is in force.
Shareholder funding may never be credited to a revenue account, and spending project funds may never debit a shareholder loan account.
A non-shareholder funder may not be credited to 221xxx or 222xxx; 211090 with a counterparty is the only permitted treatment.
Revenue may be credited only to 410001–410009.
Both legs of a cash transfer (TT-06) must be cash accounts.
The debit and credit cash accounts of a transfer may not be the same account.
Issuing an advance may not debit an expense, CIP or fixed-asset account.
When an advance is settled, the advance account must be on the CREDIT side.
Origin: File 1 Three-Level Control — posting direction restored

Rule: No expense, CIP, fixed-asset or receivable account may ever be credited in order to settle an advance.
A personal receivable (112101, 112102) requires a named individual counterparty and an approval reference.
A contract reference is mandatory on contractor advance, certification, retention and payment entries above the approved threshold.

On save, the system tests the entry against posted entries on amount + counterparty + period, on source reference, and on amount + near date (±7 days). A match raises a duplicate flag that must be dispositioned before posting.
Origin: File 1 Duplicate Test / Direct Fund Duplicate Review

Rule: Cumulative certified value may not exceed contract value plus approved variations.
Cumulative advance recovery may not exceed the advance issued to that counterparty on that contract.
Retention withheld must equal the contract retention percentage applied to the certified amount.
A payment may not exceed the outstanding payable of that counterparty.
The same supplier invoice number may not be recognised twice for the same counterparty.
Project interest acquisition payments may not be posted to an expense account.
Reclassification from 116001 to 116002/116011 requires a board resolution reference.
115030 Civil Works is a non-posting parent; postings must use 115031–115039.
Transfer from CIP to the concession right and any amortization are blocked until the Commercial Operation Date parameter is set by an authorised user.
Origin: Assignment §13 — do not invent the commercial operation date

Rule: Amortization may not be posted with an effective date before the commercial operation date.
Depreciation and amortization runs may execute only in an open period and only once per period per asset class.
Every revenue line must carry a government-share eligibility flag.
The share percentage is read from the parameter table with its effective date. It may not be hardcoded or entered on the transaction.
The share base excludes funding, shareholder loans, asset disposals, refunds and any revenue line flagged not eligible; every exclusion requires a documented reason.
Every accrual must carry a reversal period or an explicit settlement plan.
Release of a prepayment may not exceed the carried balance of that prepayment.
Any posting to 112090 automatically opens an exception record with a responsible user.
Clearing 112090 requires a resolution reference and closes the linked exception.
A reclassification may not credit an advance account a second time; the correction posts Dr correct account / Cr the account originally debited.
A reclassification may not change the amount, transaction date, description or source reference of the original entry.
A posted entry is corrected only by reversal or adjustment, each carrying a reason and a link to the original.
A reversal must post into an open period; reversing into a closed period is rejected.
The year-end result transfer is permitted only after the final close of the last period of that fiscal year.
A migration entry carries an immutable source file and source row reference and may not be created after the go-live cut-off.
Every financial statement figure must be derivable from report_mappings and the general ledger. No report figure may be stored, typed or overridden.
The trial balance must prove total debit = total credit on every run; a balancing plug is never generated.
The Cash Position book balance is always computed from posted transactions; it may never be entered.
A cash reconciliation requires the actual balance, the source document, the responsible accountant and the reconciliation date; a non-zero variance leaves the account unreconciled.
An exception may be closed only with a resolution and a resolver; it may never be deleted.
Changes to the Chart of Accounts require approval and are written to the audit log with previous and new values.
